nytimes_articles.abstract:
SOME culinary practices are most often pursued in private. One such habit, indulged in by many a fan of haute cuisine when no one else is watching, is pouring bottled salad dressings on food. Italian dressing, for example, often finds its way onto grilled steak, while blue cheese dressing frequently tops potatoes or green beans. 

     This sub rosa practice persists because, despite its lack of elegance, it has two stellar virtues to recommend it: it is drop-dead easy, and it tastes good. So, in these hot days of the salad season, when we want cooking kept to a minimum, why not bring this culinary habit out of the closet and shine it up a bit?
